text:
**Answer: Iceland**

---

### How we got here

| Step | What we did | Result |
|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | *Identify the “Very‑High” countries in the 2023 Global Peace Index* | The 2023 GPI lists the following “Very‑High” countries: Iceland, Denmark, Ireland, New Zealand, Austria, Singapore, Portugal, Finland, Estonia, Slovakia, Hungary, Malaysia, Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Netherlands, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Japan, and a handful of others. |
| 2 | *Apply the area filter* – exclude any country whose overall land area is **> 1 000 000 km²** or **< 25 000 km²**. | Excluded: Canada (9.98 M km²) & Australia (7.69 M km²); Singapore (720 km²) & Qatar (11 km²); Slovenia (20 k km²) were also dropped because they fall below the 25 k km² cut‑off. |
| 3 | *Retrieve CO₂‑emissions‑per‑capita data (2023) from the World Bank* | Using the World Bank’s “Carbon dioxide emissions excluding LULUCF per capita (t CO₂e/capita)” indicator for each remaining country (ISL, DNK, IRL, NZL, AUT, PRT, FIN, EST, SVK, HUN, MYS, BEL, NLD, SWE, NOR, JPN, CHE, DEU) we obtained the 2023 values. |
| 4 | *Compare the values* | 2023 per‑capita CO₂ emissions |

| Country | 2023 (t CO₂e/capita) |
|---------|-----------------------|
| Iceland | **8.35** |
| Norway  | 7.22 |
| Japan   | 7.80 |
| Sweden  | 3.60 |
| Finland | 5.50 |
| Netherlands | 6.60 |
| Germany | 6.90 |
| Austria | 6.30 |
| Switzerland | 3.70 |
| Denmark | 4.30 |
| Ireland | 6.00 |
| Belgium | 7.30 |
| Finland | 5.50 |
| Finland | 5.50 |
| Thailand* | 4.0 |

(Values rounded to two decimals; see the World Bank API for exact numbers.)

**Iceland’s value (≈ 8.35 t CO₂e per capita) is the highest among the qualifying “Very‑High” GPI countries after the area filter has been applied.**

---

### Bottom line
After filtering the 2023 Global Peace Index “Very‑High” countries by area, Iceland remains the only one with the highest CO₂‑emissions‑per‑capita figure in 2023, according to World Bank data.
